what_it_is.prose: Tata Lockheed Martin Aerostructures Limited (TLMAL) is a joint venture between Tata Advanced Systems Limited (TASL) and Lockheed Martin Aeroframe Corporation, established in 2010 and based at the Adibatla aerospace SEZ near Hyderabad, Telangana. TLMAL is the global single source of empennage (tail) assemblies for the C-130J Super Hercules and LM-100J — every new Super Hercules built at Lockheed Martin's Marietta, Georgia line is fitted with a TLMAL-built empennage. The JV had delivered its 200th empennage by August 2023 and more than 220 by September 2024. TLMAL also produces the C-130J centre wing box and, since a March 2023 agreement, F-16 fighter wings for Lockheed Martin's global requirements: the first Made-in-India F-16 wing — a fuel-carrying, 9G, 12,000-hour interchangeable wing with over 70% of parts sourced from Indian industry — was certified by Lockheed Martin on 7 December 2021. The facility, which employs roughly 650 people, houses India's first metal-to-metal bonding line (4,700 sq m, opened April 2018). TLMAL sits at the centre of Lockheed Martin's 'Make in India' aerostructures strategy: it underpins the F-21 offer to the Indian Air Force and, via a September 2024 teaming agreement between Lockheed Martin and TASL, a planned C-130J MRO facility for the IAF's 12 Super Hercules and future Medium Transport Aircraft (MTA) assembly in India.

deployments_procurement.summary: TLMAL is a build-to-print / co-production aerostructures supplier rather than a platform operator. Its output flows into Lockheed Martin's global C-130J and F-16 supply chains; Indian relevance is anchored by the IAF's 12 C-130J-30 fleet, the proposed in-country C-130J MRO, and Lockheed's F-21 fighter offer to the IAF.

faq.question: What does TLMAL manufacture?
faq.answer: Tata Lockheed Martin Aerostructures Limited (TLMAL) is the global single source of empennage (tail) assemblies for the C-130J Super Hercules and LM-100J — every new Super Hercules built in Marietta, Georgia flies with a TLMAL empennage. It had delivered its 200th empennage by August 2023 and more than 220 by September 2024, at roughly 24 per year. TLMAL also builds the C-130J centre wing box and F-16 fighter wings for Lockheed Martin's global supply chain.

faq.question: Who owns TLMAL and where is it located?
faq.answer: TLMAL is a joint venture between Tata Advanced Systems Limited (majority partner) and Lockheed Martin Aeroframe Corporation (minority), formed in 2010. It operates from the Adibatla aerospace SEZ near Hyderabad, Telangana, employing about 650 people and housing India's first metal-to-metal bonding facility (opened April 2018). The exact equity split is widely reported as roughly 74:26 but was not confirmed against a primary source in this build.

faq.question: What is significant about the Made-in-India F-16 wing?
faq.answer: On 7 December 2021 Lockheed Martin certified the first F-16 fighter wing built by TLMAL in Hyderabad — a fuel-carrying, 9G, 12,000-hour interchangeable/replaceable wing with over 70% of detailed parts sourced from Indian industry. It demonstrated that Indian industry can produce flight-critical fighter primary structures and underpins Lockheed Martin's F-21 offer to the Indian Air Force.
